subject: Unexpected throttling observed — request for SLA review & evidence pull
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightshore.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@brightshore.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent throttling seen in ingestion pipeline — help confirming SLA window

Irene,

We're seeing recurring throttling-related 503s and long tail-latency spikes on our ingestion route (project: bs-prod-ingest) between ~08:42 and 09:05 PDT today. Affected customers are intermittently failing to index events — total error rate spiked to ~18% for that 23-minute window.

Can Redwood confirm any capacity events or throttling rules that would explain this? Specifically:
- Whether there was a service-side throttling/queuing event or autoscale delay on the us-west-2 serving pool
- Any operator-initiated config changes between 08:30–09:15 PDT
- Whether this window would be eligible for SLA review/credit and request for logs audit

We need:
1) Confirmation of an incident/downtime window if applicable
2) A pull of request-level logs (X-Request-Id) and a CSV timeline so we can correlate on our side

Happy to share example request ids; attaching a short timeline from our monitoring (first pass). Thanks for quick eyes on this — we have execs asking for next steps.

--
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Reliability | BrightShore Analytics
samira.khan@brightshore.com
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightshore.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:28:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throttling seen in ingestion pipeline — help confirming SLA window

Hi Samira — thanks for the details and the timeline. I’m escalating this to our SRE team now and will start a logs pull for the 08:30–09:20 PDT window to include request headers, 502/503 flags, and autoscaler events.

Quick asks while we pull evidence: could you send 2–3 representative X-Request-Ids from failed attempts (or allow us to pull all IDs for that customer tenancy)? That will speed correlation.

I’ve looped in Marcus (SRE lead) and Monica (Customer Success) so we can coordinate: Marcus — can SRE prioritize the audit and include kernel-level GPU queue metrics if present? Monica — heads-up for CS outreach and customer communications.

We’ll share a preliminary findings pack and an initial assessment of SLA eligibility within 48 hours. If this is time-sensitive for your execs, let us know and we can expedite.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightshore.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throttling seen in ingestion pipeline — help confirming SLA window

Thanks — I pulled an initial slice and attached two artifacts: a zipped log export covering 08:40–09:10 PDT and a short CSV timeline we generated from request traces. The logs include: ingress proxy latencies, model backend queue depth samples, and autoscaler events.

Prelim findings (very high-level):
- We observed a transient queue buildup on the us-west-2 serving pool at ~08:46 that aligns with the error spike you saw.
- Autoscaler scaled additional workers, but the scale-up latencies (time-to-warm) for that pool were ~35–50s for the first new instance.
- There were no operator-initiated throttles or policy changes during the window; no config pushes in the last 24h.

Next actions we recommend:
1) Full correlation on your sample X-Request-Ids — request-level traces are present in the attached zip
2) Formal SLO review to decide if the observed queuing and scale latency rise to a breach of the contractual SLO (we will prepare the calculation)
3) If eligible, draft a remediation plan and (if applicable) a service credit calculation for the affected interval

I’ve attached: redwood_logs_20260915_08-45_to_09-30.zip (log export) and request_timeline_09-15-2026.csv.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightshore.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 14:03:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throttling seen in ingestion pipeline — help confirming SLA window

Hi Samira — following up with the deliverables and next steps. Attached are the logs and the timeline Marcus mentioned; we also created a short findings memo on the event.

Summary for BrightShore:
- Confirmed observable queueing on the us-west-2 serving pool between 08:46:12–08:57:03 PDT on 2026-09-15 that maps to elevated 5xx/error rates on your tenancy.
- Root cause (prelim): transient workload surge combined with slower-than-expected scale-up latency in that specific pool. No manual throttles or policy changes detected.
- SLA implication: we are performing the SLO calculation (per section 4.2 of the MSA). Based on initial measurement, the window is a candidate for an SLA impact review; final eligibility requires aligning on the exact affected request set (we need final confirmation of the X-Request-Ids you want us to evaluate).

What we need from BrightShore to complete the assessment:
- Confirm the list of X-Request-Ids to include in the SLO calculation (we can accept a sample of up to 500 ids or permission to include all tenancy IDs for that window)
- Any downstream business impact notes that should factor into remediation prioritization

Planned timeline:
- If we get the IDs by end of day today (9/17), we can deliver a formal eligibility statement and provisional service credit estimate by end of day Monday (9/20).
- We'll follow with a post-incident review and a remediation plan within 5 business days.

Links:
- Preliminary findings doc: https://drive.redwood.internal/notes/BRIGHTSHORE-incident-20260915
- HubSpot ticket: HS-52384

Monica will coordinate customer comms and next steps on the account side. Thanks for the quick coordination — let us know if you prefer a short call to walk through the artifacts.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

-----
Attachments referenced:
- redwood_logs_20260915_08-45_to_09-30.zip (log export: ingress, backend queue samples, autoscaler events)
- request_timeline_09-15-2026.csv (CSV: timestamp, request_id, status_code, latency_ms)
